methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $2.0B total raised proxy.

private.name: Meter
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series C)

data.narrative:
ICON is a Series C-stage company in Housing & Construction that has raised $450M+ to date. The comparable universe is limited, consisting of one identified private peer (Meter) and no listed public companies, reflecting the nascent state of the frontier construction technology sector.

The stage-progression method is the applicable valuation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($450M+) as a proxy for baseline valuation and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement yields an implied valuation of $3.4B. This method assumes that ICON's trajectory aligns with standard venture capital progression patterns in the sector, though the single-method reliance introduces material limitation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $2.9B to $3.9B, with a median point of $3.4B. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the stage-progression multiplier absent a robust comparable set, the adequacy of total raised as a valuation proxy in an immature sector, and the lack of revenue or unit economics data to validate growth assumptions. The comp universe's thinness—one private peer, zero public benchmarks—constrains confidence in any point estimate. Further diligence on ICON's unit economics, capital efficiency, and market traction would be required to narrow this range materially.
